clue.text: Alleged killer tan Her Majesty sports, with A&E, for once, not needed

indicators.note: to sport something is to display it in a new guise, so the letters are worn in a fresh arrangement
one E (just once, not both) can be dropped from the letters of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written, from A&E
taken as written, from A&E

explanation.surface: A suntanned Queen shows off, and for once the hospital's casualty department is not required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not needed' with 'for once' removes one of the two Es from TAN HER MAJESTY; the A of A&E is added, and 'sports' shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanratty was hanged in 1962 for the A6 murder, though his guilt was long disputed, hence a supposed murderer.

clue.text: Two articles about daughter into running quite slowly

indicators.note: the two articles sit either side of, around, the daughter

parts.note: AN and AN, two indefinite articles

indicators.note: running suggests something in motion and disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair of newspaper pieces about someone's daughter who has taken up jogging at a gentle pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the two articles surround D; 'running' is the anagram signal, not the musical pace it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking, a little quicker than andante, meaning a moderately slow pace.

clue.text: An abrasive comedian

definitions.meaning: a gritty powder of corundum used for polishing, as on a nail board
Dick ..., British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s

explanation.surface: A rude, abrasive stand-up comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a British television comedian, known for his character sketches.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a polishing grit and the surname of a famous comic performer.

clue.text: Agitated by appearance of some white hairs?

parts.note: read the entry as an instruction: three letters taken up, i.e. reading upwards in this down clue, give TEH, which appears in whiTE Hairs

explanation.surface: Someone stressed out by spotting their first grey hairs.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the entry split as HET plus 'up' says 'write HET upwards', which gives TEH, a run of letters seen in 'white hairs'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase for being worked up, flustered or anxious.

clue.text: Deputy's short cut

definitions.meaning: a close haircut made with the number 2 clipper guard

explanation.surface: A deputy taking a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbers' clippers have numbered guards; a 'number 2' leaves the hair very short.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase serves for the person ranked just below the boss and for a cropped hairstyle.

clue.text: Some of the cell numbers American does care about

indicators.note: about signals turning the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: A prison warden's census: an American who cares about the inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DOES CARE as REACODES, after A for American. Cell here means a mobile phone, not a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialling prefixes form the opening digits of a phone number, so they are part of every mobile number.

clue.text: Hat-wearing model? That's right

indicators.note: the hat goes on, around, the model, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
the Model T Ford gives T

explanation.surface: A fashion model in a hat, and that's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE as slang for a hat is old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal claim or entitlement to something, as in a claim of ownership to land.

clue.text: A Trump lie's non-malignant? It's a killer

parts.note: Donald Trump: one of the Trumps is a Donald

indicators.note: malignant suggests something twisted and harmful, so the letters are distorted

explanation.surface: A question whether a falsehood by Trump is harmless, with a jab that it is deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malignant' rearranges LIE'S NON as NEILSON. Donald Neilson, the 'Black Panther', murdered four people in 1970s England.
explanation.definitionFit: Neilson was convicted of several murders in the 1970s, so he is a murderer.

clue.text: Killer piano in Prince cover potentially, if you were to do this

parts.words: piano in Prince cover potentially, if you were to do this
parts.note: read the entry as an instruction: doctor, i.e. rearrange, the letters of the surname and you could get PRINCE wrapped round P for piano

explanation.surface: A musician recording a Prince cover version with a piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'doctor' as a verb means tamper with, and doing it to CRIPPEN gives P inside PRINCE. Crippen was hanged in 1910 for poisoning his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawley Crippen, an American doctor in London, was executed for murdering his wife, making him a notorious murderer.

clue.text: Bit left over is not even intended for broadcast

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A leftover programme scrap that was never meant to be aired.
explanation.definitionFit: A remnant or odd scrap remaining after the rest has been used or sold.

clue.text: Most are recycling one sort of plastic

indicators.note: recycling reprocesses material into something new, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: Most people recycle one kind of plastic waste.
explanation.walkthrough: Plastic here means a payment card: Maestro was a debit card brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is slang for bank cards, and Maestro was a widely used debit card brand.

clue.text: Bug? There's a small number in a place over the pond

indicators.note: the small number goes inside the American place, as the clue says

parts.note: NY, New York, a place across the Atlantic from Britain
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: An insect question: there is a small count of them in an American spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the pond' means across the Atlantic, in America; Bug is the verb, not the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or pester them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Now touring Channel Islands, knowing about things in advance

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: the present is now

explanation.surface: Visiting Jersey and Guernsey now, with foreknowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Having foresight, able to perceive events before they happen.

clue.text: Airdrie resident's more in need of liquid refreshment

definitions.text: more in need of liquid refreshment

indicators.note: the 's reads as 'has' or 'holds', so the words contain the run of letters

explanation.surface: A man from Airdrie, a Scottish town, is thirstier than most.
explanation.walkthrough: Airdrie is a town near Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: thirstier, wanting a drink more.

clue.text: Dissident wanting official employment upset relatives

parts.note: REF is short for referee, a match official
use and employment both mean application

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A dissident wanting a government job upset family members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns KIN to NIK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet citizen refused emigration, and by extension anyone protesting against authority.

clue.text: Nice area street map's showing in red, with nothing cut out

indicators.note: the map appears inside the other letters
out means awry or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of red and cut, with O (zero, nothing) among them
an A-Z is a British street atlas

explanation.surface: A street map shows an area marked in red with nothing deleted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' mixes RED, O and CUT into COTEDUR, and 'showing in' sets the map intact inside it. Nice is the French city; an A-Z is a British street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Riviera, the coastal region where the city of Nice lies.

clue.text: Spooner's music teacher? He's six feet under!

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: rock is a style of music
a coach is a tutor or teacher

explanation.surface: A dead music teacher, buried six feet down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six feet under' means buried, but here it describes an insect with six feet that scuttles under things.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect has six legs and lurks beneath floors and furniture, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Pigment? Unknown number to ring for its formula

definitions.meaning: a white colouring powder used in paint

definitions.text: Unknown number to ring for its formula
definitions.meaning: an unknown Z, a number N and a ring O spell ZnO, the chemical formula of the compound

explanation.surface: A pigment's formula needs a phone call to an unknown number.
explanation.walkthrough: Z is an algebraic unknown, N a number and O a ring; ZnO is the chemical formula of this compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc white is a widely used white paint colour, and the compound is also in sunscreen.

clue.text: Old fellows in charge, one wearing glasses by virtue of current position

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the glasses go around the rest, as glasses are worn on a face

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
F is fellow; FF is the plural
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Former colleagues in charge, one in spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts FFICI inside OO.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for holding something because of an office held, as in automatic committee membership.

clue.text: System for detecting characters involved in arson, repeatedly

indicators.note: the run of letters is taken from within the written-out word
repeatedly says the word arson is written out twice in a row, so a run can cross the join

explanation.surface: A detection system for a serial arsonist.
explanation.walkthrough: Write ARSON twice, ARSONARSON, and the answer appears across the join: in effect AR moves from the front of arson to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo-sounding method used to locate submarines and shoals of fish underwater.

clue.text: Tipping Point? It's where shoes may be fashionable pale yellow colour

parts.note: a last is the shoemaker's form on which shoes are fashioned, i.e. made
straw is a pale yellow shade

explanation.surface: A TV quiz host notes shoes are trendy in pale yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' reads as 'able to be fashioned'. Tipping Point is also a British TV quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: The final burden that makes a situation unbearable, like the straw that broke the camel's back.

clue.text: Letter E missing: game is lost

indicators.note: lost means confused or astray, so the letters are rearranged
missing means absent, so E is dropped from the words

explanation.surface: A lost game blamed on a missing letter E.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from GAME IS, then 'lost' rearranges GAMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, used for summation in maths.

clue.text: Punt in which to practise going on river

indicators.note: the river letter goes on after the first piece

parts.note: to wage war is to practise or carry it on

explanation.surface: A punt is a boat in which to practise on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Punt is the betting sense, not the flat boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a bet, a usage common in British English.

clue.text: Novel written using small pen

parts.note: a coop is an enclosure, a pen

explanation.surface: A novel handwritten with a small pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel is a noun: Evelyn Waugh's satire on journalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's 1938 satire on Fleet Street journalists is a well-known work of fiction.

clue.text: What happens soon after Aurora raises matter involving a Parisian

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other
in a down clue, raises means lifted, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound
UN is French for 'a'

explanation.surface: Aurora brings up an issue involving a Parisian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raises' turns the matter upwards in this down clue, and 'involving' wraps it round the French article. Aurora is the goddess of dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the dawn, and daybreak follows it, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Possibly the last newspaper with adult material

parts.note: an organ is a publication, a newspaper
Z may be the last letter of the alphabet
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: The last newspaper with adult content.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, stiff, sheer fabric made of silk or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: When drunk, mostly refuse gin shots

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word is kept, the end dropped

explanation.surface: When drunk, people usually decline more shots of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims REFUSE to REFU, and 'When drunk' rearranges REFU and GIN. Dropping two letters for 'mostly' is a generous stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated firing of guns, a collective noun for shots.

clue.text: Honour tourist that's caught male killer

parts.note: a jack is an honour card in bridge

indicators.note: the tourist catches, holds, the male

parts.note: a tripper is a sightseer, a tourist
HE is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Honouring a tourist who caught a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The unidentified Whitechapel murderer of 1888, Britain's most notorious serial murderer.
